{{short description|Theorem in symplectic geometry which generalizes Darboux's theorem}}
The '''[[Constantin Carathéodory|Carathéodory]]–[[Carl Gustav Jakob Jacobi|Jacobi]]–[[Sophus Lie|Lie]] theorem''' is a theorem in [[symplectic geometry]] which generalizes [[Darboux's theorem]].

==Statement==
Let ''M'' be a 2''n''-dimensional [[symplectic manifold]] with symplectic form &omega;. For ''p''&nbsp;∈&nbsp;''M'' and ''r''&nbsp;&le;&nbsp;''n'', let ''f''<sub>1</sub>, ''f''<sub>2</sub>, ..., ''f''<sub>r</sub> be [[smooth function]]s defined on an [[open neighborhood]] ''V'' of ''p'' whose [[differential form|differential]]s are [[linearly independent]] at each point, or equivalently

:<math>df_1(p) \wedge \ldots \wedge df_r(p) \neq 0,</math>

where {f<sub>i</sub>, f<sub>j</sub>} = 0. (In other words, they are pairwise in involution.) Here {–,–} is the [[Poisson bracket]]. Then there are functions ''f''<sub>r+1</sub>, ..., ''f''<sub>n</sub>, ''g''<sub>1</sub>, ''g''<sub>2</sub>, ..., ''g''<sub>n</sub> defined on an open neighborhood ''U''&nbsp;⊂&nbsp;''V'' of ''p'' such that (f<sub>i</sub>, g<sub>i</sub>) is a [[symplectic chart]] of ''M'', i.e., &omega; is expressed on ''U'' as

:<math>\omega = \sum_{i=1}^n df_i \wedge dg_i.</math>

==Applications==
As a direct application we have the following. Given a [[Hamiltonian system]] as <math>(M,\omega,H)</math> where ''M'' is a symplectic manifold with symplectic form <math>\omega</math> and ''H'' is the [[Hamiltonian mechanics|Hamiltonian function]], around every point where <math>dH \neq 0</math> there is a symplectic chart such that one of its coordinates is ''H''.
